segments.line: It starts on a Saturday morning, after a very long night with a controller in your hand.
You trip on the stairs, and the world blinks
When it comes back, you're outside City General, three streets away, in your pyjamas. Perfectly fine. A
Then your phone buzzes. Your first bill: two thousand, nine hundred and nine dollars, for falling down the stairs.
You fall down a few more things that morning, on purpose this time.
That's how you figure out the rules.
Whatever happens, you blink, and you're back at the hospital doors, healed.
Rule two: the bill is real.
Every line is the real price of what just happened to you, at real American hospital prices, as if you had to recover the normal way.
A broken leg gets billed like a broken leg, even if it heals in a blink.
Rule three: the bill only ever comes to you.
By ten in the morning, the number at the top of your phone says sixty- three thousand, three hundred and twenty dollars.
You have eleven dollars in your bank account.
